question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Villy Søvndal (Verts/ALE), Ana Miranda Paz (Verts/ALE), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Catarina Vieira (Verts/ALE), Maria Ohisalo (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), David Cormand (Verts/ALE), Marc Botenga (The Left), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Marco Tarquinio (S&D), Hanna Gedin (The Left), Danilo Della Valle (The Left), Manon Aubry (The Left), Chloé Ridel (S&D), Barry Andrews (Renew), Annalisa Corrado (S&D), Thijs Reuten (S&D) Subject:

On 9 June 2026, presenting the proposed 21st package of sanctions against Russia, the Commission announced a comprehensive visa ban for Russia’s (ex-)combatants, who should not be authorised to enter EU territory1. The Office of the EU Special Representative for Human Rights, in its note of 20 June 20252, documented serious international humanitarian law (IHL) and international human rights law (IHRL) violations attributable to Israeli forces. Even since the ‘ceasefire’ in Gaza, violations have continued, including with the intensification of the colonisation in the West Bank3 and the indiscriminate bombing campaign in Lebanon coupled with ethnic cleansing4. French5 and Italian6 prosecutors have also opened ‘war crime’ and ‘torture’ probes over Israel’s treatment of Gaza flotilla activists. Therefore, 1.

What justification underpins the proposed visa ban for (ex-)combatants of the Russian armed forces? Is this criterion transposable to Israeli (ex-)soldiers? If not, on what objective grounds is the distinction drawn?

Does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (VP/HR) consider that the radicalisation and desensitisation to violence of Israeli soldiers, resulting from the commission of war crimes listed in the aforementioned note, pose a security risk if they are present on EU territory?
Does the VP/HR intend to propose a similar measure for Israeli (ex-)soldiers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.7.2026) The EU has a clear position that international law must be upheld in all circumstances. There is no hierarchy of victims of human rights violations and abuses. They all deserve justice and accountability. The EU’s stance on Ukraine, the Middle East, and beyond demonstrates that the EU defends the rules, not rule-breakers. Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is a flagrant violation of the UN Charter, with serious consequences for international security and the rules based international order. The gravity of the situation has called for an unprecedented EU engagement. Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine has had widespread implications, including an aggravation of the risks and threats faced by the EU. Many Russian combatants, returning from the front were previously convicted and recruited from Russian prisons. Those combatants were radicalised by Russian tactics or have participated in war crimes themselves. Their presence constitutes a threat to the values, interests and security of the EU as a whole, as well as to the public policy or to the internal security or international relations of one or more Member States or of the EU as a whole. EU’s response to Russia’s war of aggression does not diminish EU’s focus on Gaza, the West Bank and Lebanon. On 28 May 2026 the EU adopted additional restrictive measures against extremist Israeli settlers and organisations which support them and are responsible for serious and systematic human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank1. The EU will consider additional listings whenever necessary and appropriate.
